Oreca 07 Gibson.historical_insight: The Oreca 07 became the dominant chassis in LMP2, chosen by nearly every entrant as customer teams converged on its aerodynamic efficiency and mechanical reliability.

representative_entry.significance: This entry finished second overall at the 2017 24 Hours of Le Mans, leading the race outright on Sunday morning during a period of high LMP1 attrition.

Aston Martin Vantage V8.historical_insight: Derived from the production Vantage road car, the V8 GTE competed across six seasons, featuring a bonded aluminium chassis and a naturally aspirated 4.5 litre V8 engine.

representative_entry.significance: A dominant entry that secured the 2014 LMGTE Am class victory at Le Mans and the season championship.

Porsche 911 RSR.historical_insight: Porsche continually developed the 911 platform for endurance competition, culminating in a mid engine configuration ahead of the rear axle to optimize aerodynamic diffuser packaging and tyre wear.

representative_entry.significance: The retro liveried 911 RSR claimed the LMGTE Pro class victory at the 2018 24 Hours of Le Mans during Porsche's factory GTE campaign.

Toyota TS050 Hybrid.historical_insight: The TS050 featured an 8 megajoule hybrid system powering both axles. Following years of narrow defeats at Le Mans, the platform delivered Toyota's maiden 24 Hours victory in 2018.

representative_entry.significance: This crew secured Toyota's first overall win at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018, going on to capture the 2018–2019 World Endurance Championship.

Porsche 919 Hybrid.historical_insight: The 919 Hybrid competed at the height of the LMP1 manufacturer era. Combining a turbocharged 2.0-litre V4 with dual energy recovery systems, it earned three consecutive overall Le Mans wins from 2015 to 2017.

representative_entry.significance: This lineup claimed Porsche's 17th overall Le Mans victory in 2015, the manufacturer's first overall win at the event since 1998.
